course_outline_concepts: What goes in a checkpoint: weights + optimiser state + LR state + RNG + data-iter position + grad-norm history
Sharded checkpointing: per-rank save/load, format choices (DCP, Nanotron, custom)
Bit-exact resume vs approximate resume — when each matters
Instrumentation: grad-norm, loss-by-shard, entropy, KL, throughput, GPU util; what to log at what cadence
The failure that wasn't caught: silent data-iter desync across resumes

sources.what_to_extract: Core content on checkpoint composition (weights/optim-state/RNG/data-iter/grad-history), SWA / model souping, WSD stable-phase checkpoints, validation tracking, early-stop criterion.
Sharded checkpointing under FSDP: why optim state is sharded fp32, why naive save-on-rank-0 loses shards, the distributed-checkpoint (DCP) API.
Loss-scaler state must be checkpointed under fp16; master weights stay fp32; the silent resume-bug if scaler state is dropped.
WSD stable-phase forkability — the 'checkpoint every 1B tokens, fork multiple decay runs from the same trunk' pattern that makes instrumented checkpoints load-bearing.
pre_clip_grad_norm as a first-class instrumented metric; 100x spike predicts loss spike 1-5 steps ahead.
Loss-spike mitigation stack at 70B: clipping + skip-step + embedding-norm monitoring. The instrumentation required to catch these.
Model-flow staged training — each stage is its own checkpoint gate; what gets promoted.
Multi-round RSFT checkpoint flywheel: rejection-sampling outputs from round k become round k+1 SFT data — what you must persist per round.
Start simple; overfit a single batch; check that resume produces bit-exact loss. Karpathy's 'silent failure' maxims.
